audit.why: Emerald+ 51.34% over 857 games with Pantheon owning Level 1 and Level 6 and Jayce owning 2-3 and the first-item window. That matches both kits exactly: Shield Vault at 600 range beats a gate-less cannon-Q, and Acceleration Gate reverses it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike names abilities and gives no cooldowns, so 'press the lane on every Aegis Assault cooldown' has no number attached.
audit.why: The three numbers that shape the lane: Shield Vault 13/12/11/10/9 at 600 range, Aegis Assault 22/21/20/19/18 at 400, Grand Starfall 180/165/150. Aegis Assault at 22 seconds is the longest thing he has in lane and the page correctly points at it — but 22 seconds is a genuinely large window and saying so turns vague advice into a plan. Against that, Thundering Blow at 20/18/16/14/12/10 means you get roughly one knockback per Aegis Assault, so the trade is one-for-one rather than a free window.
audit.corrected: Shield Vault 13s, Aegis Assault 22s at rank 1, Thundering Blow 20s — roughly one knockback per Aegis Assault.

audit.whatIsWrong: Seven strings across both layers call Pantheon's W 'Aegis of Zeonia'. He has no ability by that name — his W is Shield Vault. Four of those also call it 'point-click'.
audit.why: Riot's Shield Vault: 'Pantheon dashes to a target, damaging and stunning them', 600 range, 13/12/11/10/9s, flagged as a dash. 'Aegis of Zeonia' is a name from his pre-rework kit and does not exist in the game the page is describing. The second half is worse than the name: calling it point-click tells the player it is unavoidable and unpunishable, when it is a dash with travel — which is exactly why the page's own advice to Thundering Blow him out of the leap works. A player who believes it is point-click will not try. This is the same class of error as the calibration examples given for Brand and Cassiopeia.
audit.corrected: Shield Vault: a 600-range dash-stun on 13s at rank 1, not a point-click.

audit.whatIsWrong: `early` says the 'Mercury Cannon-to-Hammer swap shreds his armor'. The direction is backwards.
audit.why: Riot: from Hammer Stance the swap becomes Mercury Cannon and 'the first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist'; from Cannon Stance it becomes Mercury Hammer and that first attack 'deals additional magic damage'. The shred is the first attack after swapping INTO Cannon. The mirror page pantheon__jayce.json states the same fact from Pantheon's side, so leaving it reversed here makes the two directions contradict each other on a mechanic both pages describe.
audit.corrected: The shred is the first attack after swapping into Mercury Cannon.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aegis Assault is named as a cooldown to fight around but what it actually does is never stated, and the full layer's dontsFull[1] invents a 'W execute' he does not have.
audit.why: Aegis Assault makes Pantheon 'invulnerable to damage from the front' while he channels and strikes repeatedly. Two things follow that the page never says. First, it is directional — Shock Blast fired into his face is eaten, the same orb from the side or behind is not, so the answer is an angle rather than a cooldown wait. Second, it is a channel, and Thundering Blow is a knockback, so the knockback ends it — displacement is not blocked by a damage shield. Separately, Pantheon has no execute anywhere in his kit; the closest thing is Mortal Will empowering his next spell.
audit.corrected: Aegis Assault blocks damage only from the front and is a channel Thundering Blow's knockback ends; he has no execute.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[0].text`, `whys[0]` and `wants.foe[1]` say Mortal Will 'eats your autos' / 'blocks your autos' / can be hidden 'behind'. Mortal Will does not block anything.
audit.why: Riot's Mortal Will: 'Every few spells or attacks, Pantheon's next spell is empowered.' It is a stack counter that empowers his next cast — no auto-attack block anywhere in it. The block belonged to Aegis Protection, the passive of pre-rework Pantheon, which is the same era as the 'Aegis of Zeonia' name this page uses seven times. So the page is describing a champion who has not existed for years, and the practical cost is that a Jayce is told his Level 1 auto-attacks are worthless when they are not — he gives up the auto trade he could have taken. The real Level 1 reason Pantheon wins is Comet Spear's 575 range against a gate-less cannon-Q, which the same strings already say.
audit.corrected: Mortal Will empowers his next spell every few casts; it blocks nothing, and the Level 1 edge is Comet Spear range alone.

notes: 'Aegis of Zeonia' is Pantheon's pre-rework W name and appears seven times across this matchup — it is a fabricated name in the same class as the 'Ares of Blaze' and 'Jag'talon Slash' calibration cases. His W is Shield Vault. Four of those strings also called it 'point-click', which is worse than the name: it is a dash with travel time, which is the entire reason the page's own Thundering Blow advice works. I corrected all seven plus the full-layer dontsFull entry that invented a 'W execute' Pantheon does not have. One item I left: `late` and `spikes[3].text` refer to 'his Aegis Assault cooldown' — that name is correct (it is his E) and the advice is sound, so I only added what the ability actually does, in `mid`. Third error, same vintage: three strings claim Mortal Will blocks or eats your auto-attacks. It does not — it empowers his next spell. Blocking autos was Aegis Protection on pre-rework Pantheon, which is the same era as 'Aegis of Zeonia'. This whole matchup was written against the 2018 kit.
